content.name: p
children: The operator's safety model — serialized reconciliation, conflict detection, failure-aware retry, and transactional apply — is stable and tested in CI. The API surface, scale ceiling, and operational guidance have known gaps.

children.name: li
children: All changes execute in a single PostgreSQL transaction (all-or-nothing).

children.name: li
children: Reconciliation is serialized per database target: in-process locking within a replica, PostgreSQL advisory locking across replicas.

children.name: li
children: Conflicting policies (overlapping ownership claims) are rejected, not silently merged.

children.name: li
children: Transient operational failures use exponential backoff with jitter.

children.name: li
children: Invalid specs, conflicts, and unsafe role-drop workflows fall back to the normal reconcile interval without hot-looping.

children.name: li
children: Validate reconcile performance at your target object count before relying on the operator for large role and schema inventories.

children.name: li
children: Advisory locks enable multi-replica deployment, but there is no documented HA pattern, replica guidance, or failure-mode analysis.

children.name: li
children: The operator re-applies passwords when the source Secret changes, but cannot detect a password changed directly in the database. See
for why PostgreSQL makes this undetectable.

children.name: li
children: Treat managed-provider detection as environment-specific. Verify behavior against your target RDS, Cloud SQL, AlloyDB, or Azure PostgreSQL instance before relying on provider-specific SQL planning.

the chart's RBAC to a single namespace. Ephemeral request and approval
